messages.subject: Potential instruction - cause of jaw-crusher failures (Marldale)
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Dr Petrie,

We act for a quarry operator in a dispute over a mobile jaw-crushing plant that has suffered repeated toggle-seat and eccentric-shaft bearing failures and has never achieved its warranted throughput of 320 t/h (best sustained ~210 t/h). We'd like to instruct you to report on the cause - in particular whether the failures point to under-specification of the jaw assembly, or to feed material / operation as the supplier alleges.

Are you available, and what is your day rate? This may become a single joint expert appointment.

Kind regards

Tom Gallagher
Associate | Litigation
Whitfield Carter LLP
22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
T +44 (0)20 7946 5500

Confidential and may be legally privileged.

messages.subject: RE: Potential instruction - cause of jaw-crusher failures (Marldale)
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Tom,

Yes, I can assist - this is squarely within my field. My rate is £1,450/day. To form a view I'll need the plant diary, the field service reports, the PLC tonnage/availability export, the feed gradings and the OEM jaw-assembly drawings if obtainable. Bearing failures at ~190 hours, as you describe, would be very early and tend to suggest specification or assembly rather than feed, but I'd want to see the data before committing.

Regards
Ian Petrie
Carrick Plant Engineering Consultants
